class_guess: Bell eats counter: BECv1 tm108 twin (E1) with 3-cell counter digits and a grid-shifting eat
summary: BECv1 tm108 twin (E1): 3-cell binary counter, unary, marker; rounds ruled (99.7%), the grid-shifting eat is open
mechanism: Tape: counter W of 3-cell units (0 = 000, 1 = 100, spacer 010; MSB left), unary (010)^b, marker 00, then (101)^c. Only E1 differs from tm108: B carries, so digits are 3-cell units.
Each round the marker steps one unit left (b-1, c+1) and W += 1 (B carries over 100 and spacers, turns at 000); an overflow adds a 3-cell digit at the left end.

At b = 0 the marker eats W: the 3-cell grid shifts by one cell (1-digits -> spacers, spacers -> 001), c becomes the new unary, the marker is reborn at the right, then mini-eats re-align W. N ~ (4t)^(1/3); no halt to 1e10.

rules.name: R1 A over spacer (= BECv1 HR1)
R4 carry over digit 1
rules.cases: E1 = 1LB hands the carry back to B (tm108: E keeps carrying)

rules.name: R6 overflow at the left end
ROUND: one counter increment
rules.cases: W over {010,000,100}, ends in a digit; W = U 000 V with V in {010,100}* (s, o = counts in V): inc(W) = U 100 V' (V' = V with 100 -> 000); no 000 in W: inc(W) = 100 V'. Holds for 870,221 of 872,741 K-to-K transitions from blank to 1e10 (0 mismatches)

rules.name: OVERFLOW: one counter period, left record to left record
rules.cases: W over {111,101} (all digits carried), D = number of 111 units, b > 2^D. From blank: 2,382 of 2,382 in-epoch left-record pairs to 1e10; c = 2^D-1 at 2,911 of 2,919 clean left records

rules.name: EAT shape (b = 0), aligned W: no halt, next K reached
rules.to: 0^inf W' 010^b' A> 101 00 101^c' (r') 0^inf, marker reborn at the right end
rules.cases: Shape check only (no halt, a K-moment follows). W' is W re-read on a grid shifted by one cell (100 -> 010, 000 -> 000, 010 -> 001) plus local changes; exact form not ruled

rules.name: EAT cascade: exact rule (open)
rules.from: eat with 001 units (shifted segments) and pseudo-markers
rules.cases: 2,186 eat/mini-eat transitions and 334 carries into shifted segments to 1e10 are not covered by any exact rule yet

template.note: The right half is identical: tm108's HR1, HR2, HR3 and HE2 (w0 = 101, w0' = 010, w1 = 00) hold here as R1, R7, R3 and R8. The left counter is not: in tm108, E carries over single-cell digits and m0 = 00 separates the counter from the unary. Here B carries (R4), digits are 3-cell units mixed with 010 spacers, and the eat shifts the grid, so solve_BECv1 (and its fixed-width LeftBinaryCounter) cannot apply.

strategy: Not ready for a proof. Next: rule the eat as a transducer on the counter word: the one-cell grid re-read (100 -> 010, 000 -> 000, 010 -> 001), then the mini-eat cascade until W is aligned again. Then look for a regular invariant on such words (BECv7/BECv8 carry-head and two-track transducer proofs are the closest style).
risks: The eat cascade is long and context-dependent: random {010,000,100,001} words with no 100-001 pair still halt in about 5% of trials, so the invariant must be finer than unit bigrams.
The eat consumes the counter's bit pattern at eat time (about N mod 2^D). If safety depends on those bits, this becomes arithmetic (cryptid protocol).
Proof size: likely a BECv7/BECv8-class file (tens of KB), not a one-line certificate.

checkpoint_questions.text: eat_closeup_19500: each zigzag is one round. Does the right turning point (the 00 marker) move left by about 3 cells per round while the left turning points follow a binary-counter pattern, until they meet (the eat) and the head runs to the right end?

Proof route: the counter, unary and marker are BECv1-like and ruled (99.7% of rounds to 1e10). The eat shifts the 3-cell grid and needs a transducer argument (BECv7/BECv8 style). Spend one more ~2 h stage ruling the eat, or park #29 as STUCK and move on?
Sibling R2 (F0 = 0LD) passes the counter rules R1, R3, R4 and R5 but fails the marker step R7. Should we analyse #29 and R2 as one family (shared eat analysis), or keep them separate?
